correctness.rationale: For every exact prime power the known Ramanujan formula determines an explicit integer block decomposition. At exponent one it is pI_(p-1)-J_(p-1); at higher exponent it is p^(e-1) times pI_p-J_p in h=p^(e-2)(p-1) disjoint blocks. Determinantal divisors give their complete Smith factors integrally, including zeros. Chinese-remainder factorization is an integer permutation/tensor identity; tensoring unimodular transformations and sorting local prime valuations gives every global invariant factor. Independent SymPy Smith computations matched 39 moduli, but the proof, not the finite test, establishes all integers n. Boundaries n=1 and p=2 are explicitly handled.

evidence: Published complete full-circulant Smith theorem gives rank phi(n) at all n and local p^{e-1}(pI_p-J_p) blocks repeated p^{e-1} times.
The new matrix instead has only p^{e-2}(p-1) such local blocks at e>=2 and is nonsingular exactly for squarefree n.
Published divisor-indexed Gram and reduced-divisor matrix Smith theorems explicitly restrict scope to divisor indices.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The stronger-looking all-modulus theorem for the full circulant is not stronger under unit principal-submatrix restriction: Smith invariants are not invariant under deletion of rows and columns. The present rank drops at nonsquarefree n; the exact new torsion group requires separately computed local block multiplicities and CRT assembly. Its numerical formula agrees with the full-circulant nonzero factors when n is squarefree; this special coincidence is acknowledged rather than presented as a wholly unrelated theorem.

originality.rationale: Three directly relevant published Smith classifications and foundational Ramanujan primary papers were compared by exact indexing, dimensions, prime-power local blocks, and claim implication. No inspected source yields the all-modulus unit-by-unit difference Gram Smith form; full circulants have different nonsquarefree rank and divisor-indexed matrices are distinct. The result uses classical identities and known Smith reductions, and equivalent coverage in unindexed general literature is a residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed previous theorem about arbitrary induced submatrices of Ramanujan convolution could imply this result.

The prime-power Smith computation is elementary and shares methods with the published full circulant theorem; priority of the resulting natural restricted classification requires future independent literature assessment.
The squarefree specialization has numerically identical nonzero Smith factors to the full circulant; novelty lies principally in the all-modulus unit-restriction rank/torsion law.

value.rationale: The unit positions form the canonical primitive sampling subset of a cyclic Fourier system. Determining when its integer Gram loses rational rank is a natural and nontrivial reconstruction question: nonsingularity is exactly squarefreeness. The complete invariant factors, free cokernel rank and torsion structure go materially beyond the known full-circulant spectrum and unrestricted Smith data; the result is an all-modulus structural classification, not a small sample or arbitrary unmotivated cutoff.
